- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) and forecast is rising steadily, cap upward momentum after 3–5 consecutive days of growth to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) and forecast is falling, avoid sharp downward drift; allow slight lagged rebound if sentiment reverses.
- If true outcome shows sharp spike or drop after a flat period, model should adjust forecast slope to reflect sentiment volatility, not just historical trend.
- For 30-day horizons, if true outcome deviates >10% from forecast mid-horizon, reweight recent sentiment (last 5 days) more heavily than older sentiment.
- If forecast is flat or slowly rising while sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.33), reduce forecast slope to avoid overconfidence in trend continuation.
- When sentiment history shows repeated reversal (e.g., +0.67 → -0.33 → +0.67), model should not assume linear continuation; introduce mean-reversion buffer around 1–2 standard deviations from recent mean.
